findings.title: Terminality and journal advancement are not enforced across existing Run objects
findings.reproduction: Keep original Run alive after checkpoint; construct resumed Run; verify an externally created checkpoint with sealed payload=[] through resumed Run. It retains CORRUPTED_CHECKPOINT. Then original.perform(schedule[0], synthetic_transport) succeeds.
findings.observed: One later transport call and START/COMPLETE occurred despite CORRUPTED_CHECKPOINT already on disk. Original state remained RUNNING with no local integrity events. A new restart correctly rejected the disk incident, but only after collection had continued.
findings.additional_reproductions: After one object completes schedule[0], the stale original executes schedule[0] again. Separately, a resumed object constructed before journal advancement successfully verifies its stale checkpoint and repeats that completed call. New restarts subsequently reject both duplicate histories with SCHEDULE_POSITION_MISMATCH.
findings.scope: Ordinary public Run/resume usage with two objects sharing a directory; no repository mutation, monkeypatching or concurrent threads required.

findings.title: Post-return control-flow exceptions escape without retaining terminal invalidity
findings.reproduction: Synthetic transport returns otherwise valid success fields and a bound plain-dict receipt containing a list subclass whose __iter__ raises KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit, GeneratorExit or custom BaseException. Serialization during transport_outcome raises after the callback has returned.
findings.observed: All four cases propagated the exception with zero retained incidents, RUNNING state, one attempted call and an open START. After catching it, the next scheduled transport and START/COMPLETE succeeded. New restarts later detected SCHEDULED_CALL_OMITTED_WITHOUT_FAILURE_RECEIPT.
findings.scope: Exposed transport-result validation boundary. Direct callback exceptions were retained correctly; exceptions arising during validation of returned nested values were not.

findings.title: Mutable cached schedule and gold can diverge from the protected package
findings.schedule_reproduction: Replace cached schedule[0] with seed=0 and recompute its request hash. perform accepts it and sends seed=0 despite the unchanged original frozen schedule binding. Separately, the transport callback changes its received row['seed']; that row aliases package.schedule. Subsequent collection and final_report still succeed.
findings.gold_reproduction: Change only cached member.gold from 2051-05-22 to 2051-05-23. package.verify succeeds and wire bytes remain unchanged. Returning 2051-05-23 scores semantic_correct=true and false_clean=false; against the unchanged frozen member it scores semantic_correct=false and false_clean=true.
findings.scope: Public Package/Run caller boundary; callback schedule mutation requires only the provided row reference, not arbitrary runner-code replacement. This is not a claim of protection against arbitrary Python code execution.
